To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we develop a framework to realize quantum network algorithms with prior knowledge about the network structure, and that in this framework one can perform quantum search algorithms that have arbitrarily large polynomial speed-up compared to the quantum algorithm that neglects this knowledge.

we developed an algorithm for searching a network that includes prior knowledge about the network, and showed that the algorithm is exponentially better than a naive search algorithm that neglects the prior knowledge.

we develop a quantum network search algorithm that exploits the prior knowledge about the network structure and we show that this algorithm has arbitrarily large polynomial speedup over the quantum search that does not exploit the prior knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of quantum algorithms that can be implemented on a network of quantum nodes.
the development of a framework for realisation of quantum network algorithms using prior knowledge about the network structure.
quantum algorithms that use prior knowledge about the network structure to achieve an arbitrarily large polynomial speed-up.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quantum network algorithms with prior knowledge about the network topology can be performed in a polynomial time in the number of nodes and the number of different types of edge.
quantum network algorithms can be used for quantum search with arbitrarily large polynomial advantage compared to classical search, if we have prior knowledge about the network structure.
the quantum search algorithm with the prior knowledge about the network structure has a polynomial speed up over the standard quantum search.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the quantum network search algorithm with prior knowledge can be used to solve a wide range of problems with a large polynomial speed up.
the extra phase shift can be used as an additional resource for quantum search.
quantum search with prior information about the graph structure can be performed with arbitrarily large polynomial improvement over the quantum search with no prior information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
quantum network algorithms can be significantly accelerated by the use of prior information.
quantum algorithms with prior knowledge about the network structure can have arbitrarily large polynomial speedup compared to the same quantum algorithm without prior knowledge.
quantum network algorithms that exploit the network structure are able to outperform quantum algorithms that do not.
